subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pavement Design Methods
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pavement Design Methods usable.

hook.text: How thick should a road be? Too thin and it cracks. Too thick and you waste millions.

buildup.text: AASHTO's empirical method uses the 1960s road test — results from real pavement sections.

discovery.text: Mechanistic-empirical design models stress and strain in each layer — physics-based.

twist.text: One heavy truck does the damage of 10,000 cars. Truck traffic drives pavement thickness.

climax.text: ESALs convert all traffic to equivalent 18,000-pound axle loads — the universal metric.

punchline.text: Pavement thickness is really about counting trucks, not cars.

quiz.question: Why do trucks dominate pavement design calculations?
options: Trucks travel faster and cause more surface friction
One heavy truck causes damage equivalent to thousands of car passes
Trucks use different lanes than cars, concentrating damage
